idiom_name: descriptor (__get__/__set__/__set_name__) + subscriber callbacks + plain command methods
implementation_notes: Python has no observable objects in the standard library, so the view-model is hand-built: a descriptor (or property) whose __set__ updates the private value and invokes registered callbacks is the observable property, __set_name__ makes one descriptor class serve every attribute, commands are plain bound methods or callables the view invokes, and the view (Tkinter/Textual/PySide widgets, or a template re-rendered on change) reads values and re-renders. Keep the callback list copied before notifying so a handler may unsubscribe, and notify only after the new value is stored.
pitfalls: Descriptors fire only as class attributes: assigning an instance attribute of the same name shadows the descriptor and silently disables notification.
Storing bound methods in the subscriber list keeps their objects alive; use weakref.WeakMethod when observers may die before the view-model.
Iterating the live subscriber list while a handler unsubscribes raises RuntimeError ('list changed size during iteration') - iterate over a copy.
dataclass fields and plain properties do not notify per field; pick one convention (descriptors or explicit notify calls) and keep it consistent.

variants.name: traitlets HasTraits view-model
variants.idiom_name: traitlets HasTraits: typed traits + observe callbacks + @validate cross-checks
variants.implementation_notes: traitlets - the library behind Jupyter/IPython - supplies a library-grade view-model base: HasTraits subclasses declare typed traits, observers registered with observe('name') receive old/new values, @validate enforces cross-field invariants, and hold_trait_notifications batches changes while several related traits transition together. It is the practical library route when the application already depends on traitlets (or wants validation and dynamic defaults for free); it is not a UI binder, so the view still renders from trait values on each notification.
pitfalls: Observers fire per trait: multi-field updates need hold_trait_notifications around the block or observers see inconsistent intermediate states.
A validator that forgets to return proposal['value'] silently assigns None instead of the new value.
Trait defaults are class-level unless declared with a factory; mutable defaults are then shared across instances.
Validation is not a schema: nested structures need Dict(value_trait=...) or an external validator, and failures surface as TraitError at assignment time.
